Answer: B
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates a distinct, curvilinear calcification outlining the inferior and anterior borders of the heart, which is the pathognomonic radiographic sign of constrictive calcified pericarditis. This "eggshell" calcification pattern follows the pericardial sac rather than the cardiac valves or myocardium.
